facts.text: Ford Heights was originally called East Chicago Heights and changed its name in 1987 while trying to annex the Ford Stamping Plant.
The Ford Motor Company opened a stamping plant adjacent to the village in 1956, providing equal opportunity jobs for minorities and shaping the village into a blue‑collar community.
In the late 1840s, settlers turned the area into an onion and fruit farm, marking the earliest agricultural roots before the town became suburban.
During the 1940s, local women organized to raise funds for a new fire truck, leading to the formation of the East Chicago Heights Citizens Association by 1948.
Ford Heights sits on the edge of the Tinley Moraine, a glacial landform that shapes the local landscape.
The village once served as a stopping point on the Underground Railroad, offering refuge to runaway slaves seeking freedom.
